items.note: Vidisha a great centre of orthodox religion under the Shungas and later, while Buddhism is reflected in Sanchi and Besnagar monuments; under the Guptas Vidisha a stronghold of Brahminism.
Earliest evidence of Shaivism in Madhya Bharat: Durga, Seven Mothers and Ekamukha Lingas from Besnagar, dated to the early Gupta period (4th century A.D.).
Of about 750 recorded temples in Madhya Bharat, nearly 240 are Shaiva.
Most beautiful 10th-12th century temples, including Udaypur, still enshrine Shiva lingas actively worshipped by the people.
Shaiva monastic order of the Mattamayura, with monasteries still seen at Kadwaha, Terahi and Ranod; a similar monastery at Surwaya of uncertain sect.
Heliodoros pillar inscription of 1st or 2nd century B.C. at Besnagar: a Greek ambassador from Taxila at the Shunga king's court at Vidisha became a Bhagavata and raised a Garuda pillar to Vasudeva.
A Krishna temple built at Pathari in 861 A.D. with a large pillar bearing an inscription recording this; the temple no longer exists.
Vishnu shrines number hardly 87 against the overwhelming number of Shaiva shrines and 89 Jain shrines.
Islam favoured at provincial towns of the Malwa kingdom including Bhilsa and Bhonrasa; nearly 113 old mosques on record.
Typical forts: massive walls with bastions and gates, the highest gate often called Hawa Paur; other gates named after towns they faced.
Fort occupied by the chief and garrison; civil population lived in nearby towns often enclosed by fortification walls with gates, and could seek refuge in the main fort in a siege.

items.note: Sati stones typically carry a short dated inscription naming the ruling sovereign, village and the sati; type of record bearing on dating and authority.
211 old tanks, ghats and wells in the State; a well is often a necessary corollary of a temple and ancient temples often have wells nearby.
Elaborate stepped wells with built-in apartments and flights of steps, including examples at Bhonrasa and Burro in Bhilsa District; some carry inscriptions.
Trade routes connecting north and south passed through Madhya Bharat; in ancient times Vidisha (Bhilsa), Ujjain and Mahishmati joined the western coast, the Gangetic plains and the Deccan.
